node_uv_cd_spectroscopy.title: UV-Vis Absorption & Circular Dichroism (CD) Spectroscopy
node_uv_cd_spectroscopy.subtitle: Beer-Lambert Law, Aromatic Amino Acid 280 nm Absorbance & Far-UV CD Secondary Structure Signatures

metrics.beer_lambert_law: A = \epsilon \cdot c \cdot l [where A = Absorbance, \epsilon = Molar extinction coefficient in L/(mol·cm), c = Concentration, l = Path length in cm]
metrics.protein_uv_280nm: Absorbance at 280 nm is driven by aromatic rings of Tryptophan (Trp, highest \epsilon), Tyrosine (Tyr), and disulfide bonds (Cys-Cys)
metrics.far_uv_cd_spectra: 190–250 nm region measures peptide bond backbone chirality: α-Helix exhibits double minima at 208 & 222 nm; β-Sheet exhibits single minimum at 217 nm; Random coil exhibits minimum at 195 nm

mechanism: **1. UV-VIS SPECTROSCOPY & THE BEER-LAMBERT LAW**:

• Proteins absorb UV light strongly at **280 nm** due to $\pi \rightarrow \pi^*$ transitions in the aromatic rings of **Tryptophan (Trp)** and **Tyrosine (Tyr)** (Phenylalanine absorbs weakly around 257 nm). Nucleic acids absorb strongly at **260 nm** due to conjugated double bonds in purine and pyrimidine bases.

• **Purity Ratio ($A_{260} / A_{280}$)**: Pure DNA yields an $A_{260}/A_{280}$ ratio of **~1.8**, while pure protein yields a ratio of **~0.57**. A ratio significantly below 1.8 for nucleic acids indicates protein contamination.
**2. CIRCULAR DICHROISM (CD) SPECTROSCOPY**:

• CD measures the differential absorption of left-handed versus right-handed circularly polarized light by chiral molecules. **Far-UV CD ($190\text{–}250\text{ nm}$)** probes the peptide bond backbone conformation, allowing rapid quantification of $\alpha$-helix, $\beta$-sheet, and random coil fractions during protein folding or thermal denaturation assays.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Spectroscopic Calculation Traps:

• **Calculating Concentration from Absorbance**: If a protein solution in a 1-cm cuvette has an absorbance of $A_{280} = 0.50$ and its molar extinction coefficient is $\epsilon = 25,000\ \text{L}/(\text{mol}\cdot\text{cm})$, its concentration $c = \frac{A}{\epsilon \cdot l} = \frac{0.50}{25,000 \times 1} = 2.0 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{M} = \mathbf{20\ \mu\text{M}}$!

• **Nucleic Acid Concentration Estimation**: An $A_{260} = 1.0$ corresponds to **$50\ \mu\text{g/mL}$ of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA)**, **$40\ \mu\text{g/mL}$ of single-stranded DNA or RNA**, and **$20\ \mu\text{g/mL}$ of single-stranded oligonucleotides**.
pathology: Protein Conformational Diseases (Amyloidosis / Prion conversion): Monitoring the transition of soluble recombinant PrP or tau from a native random-coil/α-helical Far-UV CD spectrum into a characteristic $\beta$-sheet minimum at 217 nm during amyloid fibril aggregation.
lab_workbench: Thermal Denaturation Midpoint ($T_m$) Determination: Monitoring ellipticity changes at 222 nm as temperature is ramped from 20°C to 95°C in a CD spectropolarimeter equipped with a Peltier thermal controller.

node_mass_spec_maldi_esi.title: Mass Spectrometry: MALDI-TOF vs ESI-MS & Proteomics
node_mass_spec_maldi_esi.subtitle: Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization vs Electrospray Ionization & Peptide Mass Fingerprinting (PMF)

metrics.maldi_tof: Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization + Time-of-Flight detector | Generates mostly singly charged ions ([M+H]+); ideal for peptide mass fingerprinting (PMF)
metrics.esi_ms: Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry | Generates multiply charged ions ([M+nH]^n+); ideal for intact large proteins and LC-MS/MS bottom-up proteomics
metrics.tandem_ms_ms: Collision-Induced Dissociation (CID) in quadrupole/time-of-flight cell fragments peptide bonds into b-ions (N-terminal) and y-ions (C-terminal) for de novo sequencing

mechanism: **1. IONIZATION TECHNIQUES (MALDI vs. ESI)**:

• **MALDI (Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization)**: Analyte is co-crystallized with an UV-absorbing organic matrix (e.g., CHCA or sinapinic acid). A pulsed UV laser ionizes the matrix, which transfers protons to the analyte to produce **singly charged ions ($[\text{M}+\text{H}]^+$)**. Ions are accelerated into a Time-of-Flight (TOF) tube where lighter ions fly faster to the detector ($m/z \propto t^2$).

• **ESI (Electrospray Ionization)**: Liquid sample is pumped through a high-voltage needle, forming a fine aerosol of charged microdroplets. Solvent evaporation shrinks droplets until Coulombic explosion releases **multiply charged ions ($[\text{M}+n\text{H}]^{n+}$)**, permitting accurate analysis of massive proteins.
**2. BOTTOM-UP PROTEOMICS & TANDEM MS/MS ($b$- and $y$-ions)**:

Proteins are digested with Trypsin (cleaves specifically at the C-terminal side of **Lysine [K] and Arginine [R]**, unless followed by Proline!). Peptides are separated by nanoflow LC and fragmented in the mass spectrometer to yield sequence-informative **$b$-ions** (retain N-terminus) and **$y$-ions** (retain C-terminus).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Proteomics & Trypsin Digestion Rules:

• **Trypsin Cleavage Specificity**: Trypsin cuts *exclusively* after **Lys (K)** and **Arg (R)**. If a peptide sequence is `AGK-PEVR-K`, Trypsin yields three fragments: `AGK`, `PEVR`, and `K`. (Remember: Proline following K or R blocks trypsin cleavage!).

• **Determining Charge State in ESI-MS**: If adjacent peaks in an ESI spectrum have mass-to-charge ratios of $m_1$ and $m_2$ (where $m_1 > m_2$ and their corresponding charge states are $z$ and $z+1$), charge $z = \frac{m_2 - 1}{m_1 - m_2}$.
pathology: Clinical Biomarker Discovery: Serum proteomics via MALDI-TOF and LC-MS/MS identifies aberrant protein expression signatures (e.g., PSA in prostate cancer or troponins in myocardial infarction).
lab_workbench: Peptide Mass Fingerprinting (PMF) Database Matching: Experimental MALDI-TOF peptide masses are matched against theoretical tryptic digests in Swiss-Prot/NCBI databases via Mascot software to identify unknown protein gel spots.

node_centrifugation_sedimentation.title: Centrifugation & Hydrodynamic Sedimentation (Svedberg Units)
node_centrifugation_sedimentation.subtitle: Differential Centrifugation, Rate-Zonal (Sucrose Gradient) & Isopycnic (CsCl Equilibrium) Centrifugation

metrics.svedberg_unit: 1 S = 10^-13 seconds (Sédimentation coefficient s = v / \omega^2 r; does not add linearly!)
metrics.differential_centrifugation: Sequential pelleting by increasing g-force: 1,000g (Nuclei/Cell debris) -> 10,000g (Mitochondria/Lysosomes) -> 100,000g (Microsomes/Ribosomes)
metrics.rate_zonal_sucrose: Particles separated by SIZE/MASS through a pre-formed shallow sucrose density gradient (5–20%)
metrics.isopycnic_cscl: Particles separated strictly by BUOYANT DENSITY in a self-forming Cesium Chloride (CsCl) gradient (Plasmids vs genomic DNA; Meselson-Stahl 15N/14N DNA!)

mechanism: **1. THE THREE MAIN CENTRIFUGATION MODES**:

• **Differential Centrifugation**: Repeatedly spinning a homogenate at progressively higher speeds and gravitational forces ($g$), pelleting crude fractions based purely on size and sedimentation rate.

• **Rate-Zonal Centrifugation (Size separation)**: Sample is layered on top of a shallow **sucrose gradient (e.g., 5% to 20%)**. Under centrifugal force, particles migrate downward at rates proportional to their **size and mass ($S$ value)**. Runs must be stopped *before* any particle reaches equilibrium density (used to separate ribosomal subunits 40S, 60S, 80S).

• **Isopycnic Centrifugation (Buoyant Density separation)**: Sample is centrifuged in a steep, self-forming salt gradient (like **Cesium Chloride, $\text{CsCl}$**). Particles migrate until their buoyant density exactly matches the density of the surrounding gradient solution (**isopycnic point**). Independent of particle size! (Used by Meselson and Stahl to separate $^{15}\text{N}$-heavy DNA from $^{14}\text{N}$-light DNA).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Centrifugation & Meselson-Stahl Rules:

• **Meselson & Stahl (1958) Semi-Conservative DNA Replication**: *E. coli* grown in $^{15}\text{N}$ (heavy band) transferred to $^{14}\text{N}$ medium. After **Generation 1**, the CsCl gradient showed **ONE hybrid intermediate band** (refuting conservative replication, which would show two distinct heavy and light bands!). After **Generation 2**, it showed **two equal bands (one hybrid, one light)** (refuting dispersive replication, which would show a single shifting intermediate band!).

• **Why does Ribosome 40S + 60S equal an 80S Ribosome?** Svedberg units ($S$) measure sedimentation velocity, which depends on mass, volume, and shape. Because two subunits pack tightly together into a smaller frictional surface area, their combined sedimentation coefficient is **non-additive** ($40\text{S} + 60\text{S} = 80\text{S}$, not 100S!).
pathology: Lysosomal Storage Disease Diagnostics: Subcellular fractionation of liver biopsy homogenates via differential centrifugation isolates enriched lysosomal fractions to assay acid hydrolase deficiencies.
lab_workbench: Plasmid DNA Isolation via Ethidium Bromide–CsCl Density Gradient: Intercalating EtBr unwinds supercoiled plasmid DNA, lowering its buoyant density relative to linear host genomic DNA in a CsCl gradient, allowing pure plasmid isolation.

node_sds_page_chromatography.title: Electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE, Native-PAGE, 2D-PAGE) & Chromatography
node_sds_page_chromatography.subtitle: Laemmli SDS-PAGE Molecular Weight Estimation, IEF Isoelectric Point & Ion-Exchange/Affinity Resins

metrics.sds_page_mechanism: Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate (anionic detergent) denatures proteins and binds at ~1.4 g SDS per 1 g protein, masking intrinsic charge and imparting a uniform negative charge-to-mass ratio
metrics.two_d_page: Dimension 1 = Isoelectric Focusing (IEF) separating proteins by pI in a pH gradient | Dimension 2 = Standard SDS-PAGE separating by Molecular Weight (MW)
metrics.chromatography_types: Ion-Exchange (DEAE [anion exchanger, binds negative] vs CM [cation exchanger, binds positive]) | Size-Exclusion / Gel Filtration (Large proteins elute FIRST!) | Affinity (Glutathione for GST-tags, Ni-NTA for His-tags)

mechanism: **1. Laemmli SDS-PAGE & MOLECULAR WEIGHT DETERMINATION**:
• Proteins are boiled in **SDS** (breaks all non-covalent bonds and coats polypeptides with uniform negative charges) plus $\beta$-mercaptoethanol or DTT (reduces and cleaves disulfide bonds).

• In an electric field through a polyacrylamide gel, proteins migrate toward the anode strictly **according to their size (Molecular Weight)**. Plotting $\log(\text{MW})$ versus relative migration distance ($R_f$) yields a straight line for estimating unknown protein sizes.
**2. CHROMATOGRAPHIC SEPARATION MODES**:

• **Ion-Exchange Chromatography (IEC)**: Separates proteins based on **net surface charge**. **Anion Exchangers** (e.g., DEAE-cellulose, positively charged) bind negatively charged proteins; **Cation Exchangers** (e.g., CM-cellulose, negatively charged) bind positively charged proteins. Eluted using salt ($\text{NaCl}$) gradients or pH shifts.

• **Size-Exclusion Chromatography (SEC / Gel Filtration)**: Porous polymer beads trap small molecules, causing them to travel a longer tortuous path, whereas **large proteins bypass the pores and elute FIRST** in the void volume ($V_0$).
• **Affinity Chromatography**: Exploits specific biological binding (e.g., **His-tag proteins** binding **Ni-NTA** metal affinity resin, eluted with Imidazole).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Chromatography & Electrophoresis Rules:

• **Size-Exclusion Elution Order Trap**: In gel filtration (SEC), **LARGE molecules elute FIRST**, and small molecules elute last! (Do not confuse with molecular sieving in gels like SDS-PAGE where small proteins migrate faster!).

• **Ion-Exchange Elution Order**: If a protein has an isoelectric point $\text{pI} = 6.0$ and is loaded onto a **Cation Exchanger (CM, negative)** at **pH 7.0**, what happens? At pH 7.0 (above its pI), the protein is **net negative** $\rightarrow$ it is **repelled** by the negative column matrix and elutes immediately in the flow-through! To bind it to a cation exchanger, you must lower the buffer pH below 6.0 (e.g., pH 4.5) so the protein becomes net positive.
• **2D-PAGE Order**: Dimension 1 separates by **pI (charge)**; Dimension 2 separates by **MW (size)**.
pathology: Protein Electrophoresis Diagnostics: Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) identifies monoclonal gammopathies (M-spikes) in Multiple Myeloma.
lab_workbench: Western Blotting (Immunoblotting): Transferring SDS-PAGE resolved proteins onto a PVDF/nitrocellulose membrane, blocking with milk protein, probing with primary antibody + HRP-conjugated secondary antibody, and visualizing via ECL chemiluminescence.

node_pcr_qpcr_taqman.title: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) & Quantitative Real-Time PCR (qPCR)
node_pcr_qpcr_taqman.subtitle: Thermal Cycling (Denaturation, Annealing, Extension), Taq DNA Polymerase, SYBR Green vs TaqMan Probes & $C_t$ Threshold

metrics.pcr_amplification_math: Theoretical Yield after n cycles = N_0 × 2^n | Amplification Efficiency E = 10^(-1/slope) - 1 (Ideal E = 100% or 2.0)
metrics.taq_polymerase: Thermus aquaticus thermostable DNA polymerase (Optimum 72°C; lacks 3'->5' proofreading exonuclease activity, yielding error rate ~10^-4 and 3'-A overhangs)
metrics.qpcr_threshold_cycle_ct: Cycle threshold (C_t) is the fractional cycle number where fluorescence crosses the background threshold line (Inversely proportional to initial template log(N_0)!)
metrics.taqman_vs_sybr: SYBR Green = Non-specific intercalator into all dsDNA | TaqMan Probe = 5'->3' nuclease assay using FRET (Reporter dye + Quencher); highly specific multiplexing

mechanism: **1. THE THREE STEPS OF STANDARD PCR THERMAL CYCLING**:
• **Denaturation ($94	ext{–}95^\circ\text{C}$, 30 sec)**: Melts template dsDNA into single strands.
• **Annealing ($50	ext{–}65^\circ\text{C}$, 30 sec)**: Allows oligonucleotide primers to hybridize to complementary sequences flanking the target region ($T_m = 2(A+T) + 4(G+C)$).
• **Extension ($72^\circ\text{C}$, 1 min/kb)**: *Taq* polymerase synthesizes new strands in the $5'\rightarrow 3'$ direction.
**2. QUANTITATIVE REAL-TIME PCR (qPCR) & THE $C_t$ VALUE**:

• qPCR monitors amplification in real time using fluorescent reporters. **$C_t$ (Threshold Cycle)** is the cycle at which fluorescence rises above background baseline. Because $N_t = N_0 \cdot (1+E)^n$, **$C_t$ is inversely proportional to the logarithm of initial template concentration**—allowing absolute quantification via standard curves or relative quantification via the **$2^{-\Delta\Delta C_t}$ (Livak) method**.

• **TaqMan FRET Mechanism**: A DNA probe carries a 5'-fluorescent reporter and a 3'-quencher. As *Taq* extends from the primer, its **$5'\rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease activity** cleaves the probe, separating reporter from quencher and generating a permanent fluorescent signal.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C qPCR & PCR Troubleshooting Questions:

• **Why does *Taq* Polymerase leave an 'A' overhang at the 3' ends of PCR products?** *Taq* possesses terminal transferase activity that adds a single untemplated Adenine (A) to 3' ends, enabling **TA-cloning** into linearized vectors with 3'-T overhangs.

• **Interpreting Melt Curves in SYBR Green qPCR**: After cycling, raising temperature gradually while monitoring SYBR Green fluorescence reveals a sharp drop (**Melting Temperature, $T_m$**) when the amplicon melts. A single sharp peak confirms a clean specific product, whereas multiple peaks indicate **primer-dimers or nonspecific amplification**.

• **Calculating Relative Fold Change ($2^{-\Delta\Delta C_t}$) $\Delta\Delta C_t$** = $(C_{t,\text{Target}} - C_{t,\text{Reference}})_{\text{Treated}} - (C_{t,\text{Target}} - C_{t,\text{Reference}})_{\text{Control}}$.
pathology: Viral Load & Cancer Diagnostics: RT-qPCR quantifies plasma HIV RNA copies/mL or BCR-ABL transcript levels in CML patients to monitor therapeutic efficacy and minimal residual disease.
lab_workbench: Colony PCR Screening: Directly dipping bacterial colonies into a PCR master mix containing gene-specific primers bypasses plasmid minipreps and restriction digestion checks.

node_sanger_ngs_sequencing.title: Sanger Dideoxy Sequencing vs. Illumina Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)
node_sanger_ngs_sequencing.subtitle: 2',3'-Dideoxynucleotides (ddNTP Chain Terminators) & Sequencing-by-Synthesis (SBS) Flow Cell Bridge Amplification

metrics.sanger_ddntp: Uses 2',3'-dideoxynucleotides lacking a 3'-OH group, causing permanent chain termination; separated by capillary electrophoresis
metrics.illumina_ngs_sbs: Sequencing-by-Synthesis using reversible fluorescent terminators and bridge PCR cluster amplification on a glass flow cell
metrics.ngs_throughput: Massively parallel generation of gigabases to terabases per run (millions of clusters sequenced simultaneously)

mechanism: **1. SANGER DIADEOXY CHAIN TERMINATION SEQUENCING**:
• Reaction mixture contains template DNA, DNA polymerase, primer, four normal dNTPs, and a low concentration of **ddNTPs** (dideoxynucleotides labeled with distinct fluorophores).

• When a polymerase incorporates a ddNTP instead of a dNTP, the missing 3'-OH prevents further phosphodiester bond formation, terminating the chain. Capillary electrophoresis separates the resulting nested set of fluorescent DNA fragments by single-nucleotide length differences.
**2. ILLUMINA NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING (NGS / SBS)**:
• **Library Preparation**: Genomic DNA is fragmented, ligated to universal adapters, and bound to a flow cell covered in lawn oligonucleotides.
• **Bridge Amplification**: Generates millions of dense clonal clusters across the flow cell.

• **Sequencing-by-Synthesis**: All four reversible fluorescently-blocked dNTPs are added simultaneously along with DNA polymerase. After imaging which cluster incorporated which color, the fluorescent dye and 3'-block are chemically cleaved off, and the next cycle begins.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Sequencing Troubleshooting & Calculations:

• **Reading a Sanger Sequencing Electropherogram**: Always read peaks from **bottom to top (5' to 3')** on a gel, or left-to-right on a capillary chromatogram. The first peak after the primer corresponds to the nucleotide closest to the primer (5' end of the newly synthesized strand = 3' end of the template!).

• **Sanger vs NGS Applications**: Sanger sequencing is gold-standard for low-throughput single-gene validation, plasmid verification, and PCR check; Illumina NGS is gold-standard for whole-genome sequencing, RNA-Seq transcriptomics, and ChIP-Seq epigenetic profiling.
pathology: Clinical Oncology Panel Sequencing: NGS panels screen tumor biopsies simultaneously for actionable mutations in *EGFR, KRAS, BRAF, BRCA1/2*, guiding precision targeted therapy.
lab_workbench: Bioanalyzer Fragment Analysis: Assessing DNA/RNA library fragment size distribution and purity prior to loading onto an Illumina flow cell.

node_confocal_frap_superres.title: Confocal Laser Scanning Microscopy (CLSM), FRAP & Super-Resolution Imaging
node_confocal_frap_superres.subtitle: Pinholes Rejecting Out-of-Focus Light, Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching & STED / STORM Nanoscopy

metrics.confocal_pinhole: Conjugate pinhole aperture in the optical path blocks out-of-focus light rays, producing sharp optical z-sections
metrics.frap_kinetics: Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching measures protein lateral diffusion coefficients (D) and mobile fraction (MOBILE vs IMMOBILE fractions)
metrics.super_resolution_abbe: Abbe diffraction limit (~200 nm lateral resolution) broken by STED (stimulated emission depletion) or STORM/PALM (single-molecule localization microscopy down to ~20 nm)

mechanism: **1. CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY & OPTICAL SECTIONING**:

• Standard epifluorescence microscopes collect blurry light from above and below the focal plane. **Confocal Laser Scanning Microscopy (CLSM)** uses point illumination and a conjugate **pinhole aperture** placed in front of the detector to reject all out-of-focus light, yielding crystal-clear optical z-stacks.
**2. FRAP (FLUORESCENCE RECOVERY AFTER PHOTOBLEACHING)**:

• A high-powered laser beam irreversibly bleaches fluorophores within a microscopic region of interest (ROI). By recording how fast unbleached fluorescent molecules diffuse back into the ROI (**Recovery Curve**), researchers calculate the **diffusion coefficient ($D$)** and **mobile fraction** of membrane proteins or nuclear transcription factors.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Microscopy Principles:

• **Abbe Diffraction Limit Equation**: Resolution $d = \frac{0.61 \lambda}{N.A.} = \frac{0.61 \lambda}{n \sin\theta}$, where $\lambda$ is wavelength and $N.A.$ is Numerical Aperture. To improve (lower) $d$, you must use shorter wavelengths ($\lambda$) or higher $N.A.$ immersion oil objectives.

• **Interpreting FRAP Recovery Curves**: A rapid, 100% recovery curve indicates highly mobile cytosolic proteins freely diffusing; a sluggish or partial recovery curve indicates proteins tethered to the cytoskeleton or macromolecular complexes (immobile fraction).
pathology: Live-Cell Dynamics in Cancer Biology: FRAP measures aberrant stiffening or immobilization of focal adhesion and cytoskeletal proteins in migrating metastatic cancer cells.
lab_workbench: FRET (Förster Resonance Energy Transfer) Microscopy: Measuring non-radiative energy transfer between donor (e.g., CFP) and acceptor (e.g., YFP) fluorophores when within <10 nm to prove direct protein-protein interactions in live cells.

node_flow_cytometry_elisa.title: Flow Cytometry (FACS) & Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA)
node_flow_cytometry_elisa.subtitle: Forward Scatter (FSC) vs Side Scatter (SSC), Fluorophore Multiplexing & Sandwich vs Indirect ELISA

metrics.fsc_vs_ssc: Forward Scatter (FSC) is proportional to cell size/volume | Side Scatter (SSC) is proportional to intracellular granularity/complexity
metrics.facs_sorting: Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting deflects electrostatically charged droplets containing antibody-labeled cells into collection tubes
metrics.elisa_types: Sandwich ELISA (Antibody capture + Antigen + Enzyme-conjugated Detection Antibody; highest sensitivity) vs Indirect ELISA (Antigen coated + Primary Antibody + Secondary-HRP)

mechanism: **1. FLOW CYTOMETRY & FACS**:

• Cells in suspension are hydrodynamically focused into a single-file stream intersecting one or more laser beams. Detectors measure light scatter: **Forward Scatter (FSC)** measures particle size; **Side Scatter (SSC)** measures internal complexity (granularity/nuclei).

• Fluorophore-conjugated monoclonal antibodies bind specific surface or intracellular markers (e.g., CD4, CD8). Fluorescence emission is split through optical filters and photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to quantify marker expression.
**2. ELISA (ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY)**:

• **Sandwich ELISA**: A capture antibody is coated onto a 96-well plate; sample antigen binds; an enzyme-linked detection antibody completes the 'sandwich'; adding chromogenic substrate (e.g., TMB) yields a quantifiable colored product proportional to antigen concentration.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part B & C Flow Cytometry & ELISA Rules:
• **Interpreting Flow Cytometry Scatter Plots**: Lymphocytes form a distinct tight cluster on FSC vs SSC plots; dead cells and debris have extremely low FSC and high SSC (gated out during analysis).

• **Why is Sandwich ELISA more sensitive than Indirect ELISA?** Sandwich ELISA utilizes two distinct antibodies recognizing non-overlapping epitopes on the antigen, drastically reducing background noise and non-specific cross-reactivity.
pathology: CD4+ T-Cell Enumeration in HIV/AIDS: Flow cytometry monitors disease progression by quantifying absolute CD4+ T-lymphocyte counts in patient blood samples.
lab_workbench: Quantitative ELISA Standard Curve: Plotting absorbance at 450 nm versus known serial dilutions of purified recombinant standard protein to interpolate unknown serum/cell lysate concentrations.

Chaotropic agents like 8 M Urea break water structure around hydrophobic amino acid side chains, exposing buried Trp/Tyr residues and abolishing the characteristic double minima of alpha-helices in Far-UV CD spectra.

mechanism_steps.event: 5'->3' exonuclease activity of Taq polymerase cleaves hybridized TaqMan probe during primer extension

As Taq extends from the upstream primer, it encounters the downstream TaqMan probe and hydrolyzes it via its 5'->3' exonuclease domain, separating the 5'-reporter fluorophore from the 3'-quencher to produce real-time amplification fluorescence.
